claims.statement: The six shared framework targets have explicit inward build dependencies: Application depends on Domain; Persistence and Presentation on Application and Domain; Infrastructure on Persistence, Application and Domain; Remote Infrastructure on Infrastructure, Application and Domain. Both native app targets depend on all six.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests check app-target imports and selected implementation and platform imports across shared frameworks: five non-Presentation frameworks share a no-app-import list, Presentation has its own storage and platform import list, and Domain and Application receive additional restrictions; these exact-import guards are not a universal prohibition on conditional platform UI in Presentation.

Native apps assemble concrete stores and services; desktop WindowModel owns each window's workspace collection and navigation, while on mobile the shared MobileAppModel retains per-persistent-UIKit-session MobileWorkspaceSessionModel instances that own their own live workspaces and descriptors; MobileSceneModel selects within its bound session.

The MCP bridge is a separate authenticated stdio-to-HTTP executable, the widget renders ActivityKit workspace summaries, and the forwarding benchmark is a standalone shared-framework consumer rather than app/test-host logic.
AgentKit has a reference submodule checkout but Xcode declares a versioned remote package; Termind registers host-specific SSH/SFTP tools on its side of the host-neutral runtime boundary.

Cross-feature responsibility is split among Application policy, concrete shared adapters, Persistence stores and native owners: remote files use a filesystem port plus a transfer coordinator; Assistant execution uses an injected tool-registry factory; Vault sync uses persistence journals; speech uses an injected native audio input.

The reusable device directory follows the normal shared-module boundary: TermindDomain owns DeviceRecord, TermindApplication owns the repository port and observable model, Persistence owns the SwiftData implementation, and each app supplies platform-specific display-name acquisition.

TermindIOSApp is the mobile @main entrypoint, selecting live or test dependencies and constructing a MobileAppModel; MobileStartupView installs its container or displays unavailable content on initialization failure. Desktop TermindApp composes shared services for each WindowGroup, exits via the database-in-use guard when the store is occupied, and fatally terminates launch for other initialization errors.

MobileAppModel assembles persistence, connections, sync services and Agent host services, retains per-UIKit-session workspaces and exposes a flattened view for app-wide coordination; test or injected-host configuration omits live sync and disables Live Activities by default, while scene selection is scoped to its bound workspace session.

Xcode declares AgentKit as a remote upToNextMajorVersion package starting at 0.19.1 and builds the committed Package.resolved pin; edits in the reference submodule or sibling working tree alone do not change this build.

The Xcode target membership compiles WorkspaceActivitySupport source into TFI, TermindWidgets and TFITests; TFI embeds the widget extension, which directly depends on TermindPresentation, while TFM embeds the separate MCP bridge tool.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests enforce source-level dependency and ownership restrictions across shared frameworks and native features, independently of Xcode target edges, and guard the forwarding benchmark against becoming an app or test dependency.
FrameworkTests directly depends on all six shared frameworks; the platform test targets depend on their app and selected shared frameworks rather than the standalone port-forwarding benchmark.

Shared Presentation has conditional AppKit and UIKit imports for rendering despite the architecture test's exact-line import exclusions; the import guard matches only unindented `import Module` lines, so it does not prove that all shared presentation views are platform-independent.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests enforce selected import and construction restrictions on native Application, UI and Features directories rather than a universal ban on native feature imports of shared frameworks; the AgentKit shadow-declaration guard scans the desktop source tree for an explicit set of runtime type names, not every AgentKit-related type across all targets.

Device directory changes are committed to a device-kind History journal and synchronized as native DeviceItem fields by DeviceSyncCoordinator, separately from the Vault record format and journal; both apps gate device sync startup on Pro/iCloud sync eligibility.

The device directory model registers the current installation on creation, caches ID-to-name lookups and tracks storage errors; the SwiftData implementation does not resurrect a remotely deleted device on launch registration, though explicit upsert can recreate it.

Device and connection-history synchronization use separate kind-filtered engines and states in the same CloudKit zone; after remote device changes, native composition reloads the device-directory model's cache.

Mobile Assistant assembly passes AgentHostServices.live the connection coordinator and SFTP concurrency scheduler, and injects native iOS audio input into shared speech transcription with interruption cancellation.

Mobile restoration stores descriptors by persistent UIKit session ID, consolidates saved descriptors into the first bound session after a process start without connecting them, and keeps subsequent windows independent; selecting a saved workspace lazily materializes and connects it in its owning session.

Scene disconnect or view disappearance does not discard a restorable UIKit workspace session. Reconciliation uses native session IDs to detect orphans and saves new ownership before transferring live instances without reconnecting; save failures preserve prior ownership. Native discard closes that session's entries, including previously recovered instances.

Mobile workspace activity links route to the persistent UIKit session that owns the workspace rather than moving its connection to the receiving window; independent-session and recovery behavior is covered by model tests, while native-window integration tests are opt-in with TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1 and serialized execution.

TermindAgentTools composes Termind's host-aware tool catalog from injected host, connection, metrics, authentication, background, and optional scratch/pane services; mutating host tools are acting-only, absent optional capabilities omit their tools, and its presenter registry combines AgentKit built-in and Termind presenters with a closed legacy-name fallback for pre-ID transcript cards.

Xcode's remote AgentKit up-to-next-major requirement starts at 0.19.1 and resolution pins 0.19.1 at 8108c9bb87c546860cfc1769571e115af919fe8a. Resolved-only builds cannot silently advance that pin; sibling/reference checkout edits alone are not Xcode dependency changes.

libssh2 maintenance is separate from Xcode's remote exact 2.0.3-termind-4 package pin at 7ca39b8bcaf408351e8b6e4f449d2a39959bab49. Ghostty has no local maintenance submodule and is consumed directly from Lakr233/libghostty-spm with up-to-next-major 2.2.2026100501, resolved at 7199bd7aa3c32d0a5edcab7fe87b3c1e76f76de9.

libtailscale-spm is a maintenance submodule, but Xcode consumes its remote package through upToNextMinorVersion from 1.0.2, resolved to 1.0.2 at 098e6b69ea128f3a55bc560f005a3e851123dc99; TailscaleKit is a direct package product of Remote Infrastructure, not a shared framework target.

Remote Infrastructure owns the embedded userspace Tailscale node implementation; ArchitectureBoundaryTests rejects TailscaleKit and CTailscale imports in Domain, Application, Presentation, and Persistence.

Application owns TerminalFindController state and policy, with terminal actions and focus injected by native session/workspace owners. Dismissal retains query and optionally suppresses focus restoration; resize suspension prevents search/navigation until resume, which only restarts a still-presented nonempty query.

The reusable mobileToolbarSearch UIKit bridge owns native search attachment/responder transitions, defers synchronization from SwiftUI updates, fences presentation and edits during dismissal and restores the navigation owner's presentation context when removing its owned controller.

MobileWorkspaceSearchModifier owns workspace-kind search bindings in the feature layer: SSH and Telnet bind the shared Find controller and dismiss without restoring terminal focus, while SFTP binds the browser query; reusable mobile search UI does not own this workspace-kind switch.

FrameworkTests verifies terminal Find query retention, navigation without a query, and idempotent dismissal without terminal focus restoration; MobileShortcutTests verifies native Find key routing and that Escape remains terminal input unless Find is presented.
